edges.effect_quant: The clearest large-cohort signal found high-potency statin exposure associated with higher rhabdomyolysis risk in men (HR 1.93, 95% CI 1.27-2.94), with rosuvastatin 20 mg and simvastatin 40 mg showing HRs above 5 in some subgroups.
edges.population: adults prescribed high-potency or high-dose statin therapy for primary prevention or routine clinical care
edges.mechanism: Severe statin muscle toxicity is most plausible when high systemic statin exposure overwhelms skeletal-muscle energy handling, especially with higher doses, CYP3A4-interacting drugs, or impaired renal clearance.
edges.summary: The anchor study here is the French nationwide cohort, which did not show a blanket excess for all statin use but did show a clear harm signal once therapy moved into high-potency dosing. That makes this a dose-intensity safety edge more than a class effect applying equally to every statin regimen.
edges.caveats: Rhabdomyolysis remains rare, so absolute event rates are low even when relative risk rises. Sex, interacting drugs, renal disease, and specific statin-dose combinations appear to matter more than the statin class alone.

evidence.citation: Coste F 2019 Eur J Prev Cardiol
evidence.notes: Statins for primary prevention and rhabdomyolysis: A nationwide cohort study in France.
